title: Kanye's WSJ Plea To All The CEO's He's Loved Before
text:
Is Kanye really sorry and is he really healing, or just feeling left out now that CEOs have a new favorite bigot to throw their millions at?
This morning, Kanye took out a full page ad in the Wall Street Journal , revealing the longstanding impacts of bipolar disorder and tracing its origins to brain damage from a car accident 20+ years ago. He offers a groveling apology for his anti-semitism and very briefly acknowledges the “Black community” for holding him down for all these years.
If I’m being frank…“Thanks for holding me down,” especially after his last fifteen years(!) of antics, is simply not enough. It’s also not entirely accurate, because …*looks around the room*… I don’t really recall seeing many of us holding that man down.
The only Black people I’ve seen in Kanye’s orbit lately have been his security guards and maybe the choir from his Sunday Service era. His creative circle are not Black, his friends and collaborators are not Black, the inner circle he chose to staff with internet famous white supremacist incels is obviously not Black. The women he seeks out relationships with are not Black, and his fans for the most part, the ones that have followed him through the last decade have not really been Black. Mostly White, Latino, and Asian at least here in California.
Maybe he’s talking about the same Black community we saw in that Diddy doc. You know, the ones still racing to cuddle up and take selfies with Diddy even as images of him beating Cassie were already blasted across the world. The folks that Harriet would’ve left behind.
If we’re flashing back to 2016, it wasn’t a predominately Black crowd selling out every night of his Saint Pablo tour and proudly wearing his merch. You know, that tour where he spent time ranting about Black people “needing to get over racism,” and that infamous, “If I voted, I would’ve voted for Trump” bit.
In 2013, three years before, he was wearing and selling merch with Confederate flags on it. Granted, he was technically allowed to because unlike Germany and the Nazi flag, America hasn’t made flying or wearing the Confederate flag illegal or leveled any efforts to formally disavow it from American culture. Anyway, that same year, he entered a major partnership with Adidas.
He pledged his support to Trump throughout his first term, visiting the White House in 2018 after spending nearly a year wearing a MAGA hat anywhere he could. Trump’s plans to enact the terror we’re experiencing now were campaign platforms in their infancy then. The racism, sexism, xenophobia, birtherism, “shithole countries,” “build the wall,” “grab her by the pussy.”
“My MAGA hat makes me feel like Superman (2018)” … Two years later, Kanye showed up on my ballot as a 2020 Presidential candidate. He got nearly 60,000 votes across twelve states , undoubtably from a mostly young male audience in favor of hype and indoctrinated against consequence. That same year, 2018, he and his Yeezy brand were able to enter a 10-year partnership with Gap. The partnership ended prematurely after two years, but it still fucking happened. Adidas’ partnership lasted all the way to 2022, with Kanye’s contract only being terminated after he began pivoting more specifically to anti-semitism.
Adidas released a brief statement about the split, stating that the brand “does not tolerate anti-semitism and any other sort of hate speech.” They called his recent comments and actions “unacceptable, hateful and dangerous,” and said they violated “the company’s values of diversity and inclusion, mutual respect and fairness.”
This brand remained fully loyal to him through 2013’s Confederate flags and 2018’s “slavery was a choice.” But… values of diversity and inclusion, mutual respect, and fairness.
Both Gap and Adidas continued to pumping money into him even as his mania teetered into Koresh territory. Mania or not, Kanye enjoyed career success, Coachella stages, and continued partnerships as he disparaged his Black Americans. Propelled by an executive layer who didn’t respond his antics with distance or shame, but with a general unseriousness, pleasure, and even encouragement.
Universal Music Group CEO Lucian Grainge and music exec Lyor Cohen pose with Kanye. If we’re looking at the preferred formulas of men like Lucian and Lyor, Kanye’s detrimental influence to Black America is more valuable than his sanity or artistry. After all, these are men who intentionally skip over Black Juilliard virtuosos to keep pushing street level criminals and sex workers as the faces of Black music stardom. I know there’s a secret, Reagan-era handshake deal with the CIA happening there, but I can’t prove it.
So here’s today’s question… Can Kanye Brand™ recover into mass acceptance?
Everyday, we’re given opportunities as individuals and as a society to draw a line, and every day we fail.
Paris Hilton went from calling gay men f*ggots in the club to headlining West Hollywood Pride! All she had to do was blame it on trauma caused by her very straight and very white parents sending her to some wilderness camp. (She sued the website hosting the videos and had them mostly wiped from the internet).
And there’s Harry, very famous Nazi from an actual family of Nazis . All he had to do was blame it on his mother’s death, or trying to impress his brother or something, and promise to help IDF soldiers launder their brands through his charity. I think somewhere in there he (and his wife) also had to agree keep the words “Palestine” and “genocide” out of their “humanitarian” work and agendas.
I personally like to keep a hard line when it comes to Nazis…whether they say they’re sorry, or they were tricked, or they were manic, or grieving…. I’m good on that. 🤚🏾
Unfortunately for Kanye, he doesn’t have the #complexion to rebrand into innocence. And, at nearly 50 years old, I’m not sure he has the time. Who’s left to invest? Everyone who was willing to ride the risk of Kanye already made their money.
He can be a genius, he can be deluded, but at no point is providing him with an audience mandatory. Though, despite the swastikas and Confederate flags and all, there’ll always be someone willing…
His full letter below…
To Those I’ve Hurt
By Ye
Formerly known as Kanye West
Twenty-five years ago, I was in a car accident that broke my jaw and caused injury to the right frontal lobe of my brain. At the time, the focus was on the visible damage—the fracture, the swelling, and the immediate physical trauma. The deeper injury, the one inside my skull, went unnoticed.
Comprehensive scans were not done, neurological exams were limited, and the possibility of a frontal-lobe injury was never raised. It wasn’t properly diagnosed until 2023. That medical oversight caused serious damage to my mental health and led to my bipolar type-I diagnosis.
Bipolar disorder comes with its own defense system: denial. When you’re manic, you don’t think you’re sick. You think everyone else is overreacting. You feel like you’re seeing the world more clearly than ever, when in reality you’re losing your grip entirely.
Once people label you as “crazy,” you feel as if you cannot contribute anything meaningful to the world. It’s easy for people to joke and laugh it off when in fact this is a very serious, debilitating disease you can die from. According to the World Health Organization and Cambridge University, people with bipolar disorder have a life expectancy that is shortened by ten to fifteen years on average, and a 2x–3x higher all-cause mortality rate than the general population. This is on par with severe heart disease, type-I diabetes, HIV, and cancer—all lethal and fatal if left untreated.
The scariest thing about this disorder is how persuasive it is when it tells you: You don’t need help. It makes you blind, but convinced you have insight. You feel powerful, certain, and unstoppable.
I lost touch with reality. Things got worse the longer I ignored the problem. I said and did things I deeply regret. Some of the people I love the most, I treated the worst. You endured fear, confusion, humiliation, and the exhaustion of trying to love someone who was, at times, unrecognizable. Looking back, I became detached from my true self.
In that fractured state, I gravitated toward the most destructive symbol I could find, the swastika, and even sold t-shirts bearing it. One of the difficult aspects of having bipolar type-I are the disconnected moments—many of which I still cannot recall—that lead to poor judgment and reckless behavior that oftentimes feels like an out-of-body experience. I regret and am deeply mortified by my actions in that state, and am committed to accountability, treatment, and meaningful change. It does not excuse what I did, though. I am not a Nazi or an antisemite. I love Jewish people.
To the Black community—which held me down through all of the highs and lows and the darkest of times—the Black community is, unquestionably, the foundation of who I am. I am so sorry to have let you down. I love us.
In early 2025, I fell into a four-month long manic episode of psychotic, paranoid and impulsive behavior that destroyed my life. As the situation became increasingly unsustainable, there were times I didn’t want to be here anymore.
Having bipolar disorder is notable state of constant mental illness. When you go into a manic episode, you are ill at that point. When you are not in an episode, you are completely ‘normal’. And that’s when the wreckage from the illness hits the hardest. Hitting rock bottom a few months ago, my wife encouraged me to finally get help.
I have found comfort in Reddit forums of all places. Different people speak of being in manic or depressive episodes of a similar nature. I read their stories and realized that I was not alone. It’s not just me who ruins their entire life once a year despite taking meds every day and being told by the so-called best doctors in the world that I am not bipolar, but merely experiencing “symptoms of autism.”
My words as a leader in my community have global impact and influence. In my mania, I lost complete sight of that.
As I find my new baseline and new center through an effective regime of medication, therapy, exercise, and clean living, I have newfound, much-needed clarity. I am pouring my energy into positive, meaningful art: music, clothing, design, and other new ideas to help the world.
I’m not asking for sympathy, or a free pass, though I aspire to earn your forgiveness. I write today simply to ask for your patience and understanding as I find my way home.”
With love,
Ye
